signal.mechanism: Low physical inventory relative to refinery use and its prior seasonal norm may require compensation for scarcity risk in oil futures. This tests a slow state-dependent long risk premium, not V17 weekly news-change direction or an alternate weight of its seven-component composite.
signal.cover_days: 1000*current_value[Stocks,Commercial (Excluding SPR)]/current_value[Crude Oil Supply,Crude Oil Input to Refineries]; million barrels divided by thousand barrels/day
signal.baseline: For the observation month, compute mean cover_days in each of exactly five preceding calendar years, then arithmetic mean of all five yearly means. At least3valid distinct observation weeks in EVERY year/month; first published usable observation per week, already available strictly before current release. No current-year observations, later revisions or future releases in baseline; no shorter-history fallback.
signal.primary: long BR weight0.9 when current cover_days strictly below baseline and fully ready, otherwise cash; equality cash
signal.control: constant long0.9 on the same source-readiness/fill calendar; contextual baseline, never promote after outcomes
signal.availability: exact inherited conservative23:59:59America/New_York on official release date, independent of current retrieval or Last-Modified. Existing V72 EOD decision clock23:59:59.999999999Moscow, next factual open only.
signal.missing: nonpositive/nonfinite current stock or refinery use, missing selected row or incomplete baseline => newest release unready and cash, never fallback to older usable release. The excluded stale2019-07-03issue remains an unready calendar state.

Theory of storage motivates a possible link between inventories and risk premiums, not guaranteed rising spot prices. US commercial inventories/refinery intake are not global Brent inventories, demand forecasts, measured convenience yield or producer hedging risk. Seasonal maintenance, imports/exports, capacity and structural breaks may dominate the proxy. Not a replication of the cited literature.
